title: legal redlines scratchpad - customer master agreement (CMA)
content:
Quick notes / negotiation talking points — CMA (incoming enterprise customer, finance <> legal + AE loop)

Context:
- Enterprise prospect (payment terms + custom DPA requested). Wants SLA 99.9% across Dedicated + Hosted. May push for indemnity carveouts and broader data use rights.
- AE says potential ARR ~ $1.2M, strong reference value. Need to prioritize: limit liability, preserve IP/ML model protections, maintain ability to route to fallback models for reliability.

Primary clauses to watch (first pass):
1) Liability / Cap (HIGH priority)
   - Proposed customer cap: 12 months of fees or $1M (whichever greater) — current template 24 months. Push to 12 months.
   - Exclude indirect, consequential damages. Watch for carveouts (IP infringement, gross negligence).
   - If they insist on higher cap, require narrower breach categories that trigger higher cap (e.g., IP infringement only).

2) Indemnity (HIGH)
   - Customer seeking indemnity for third-party claims arising from their use of outputs. Reject broad indemnity: we can indemnify for IP infringement claims tied solely to our models/outputs, but not for customer productization or misuse.
   - Add explicit carveout: no indemnity for modifications or combined use with third-party data/libraries.

3) Data / DPA / Data Rights (HIGH)
   - They want rights to use model outputs for retraining — must not allow unrestricted model retraining or rights to our model weights.
   - Clarify: customer retains rights to their input data and factual outputs they generate for their own use, but no license to underlying model IP or derivatives.
   - KMS/HSM requirement? If requested, confirm scope: at-rest/encryption-in-use vs. key management responsibilities.

4) SLA / Availability & Remedies (MEDIUM)
   - 99.9% SLA across Dedicated + Hosted is tough for burst patterns. Consider: 99.9% for Dedicated, 99.5% for Hosted; define measurement window, exclude scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
   - Remedies: service credits only. Avoid termination right for single SLA miss. Cap credits at small % of monthly fees.

5) Security / Compliance (MEDIUM)
   - They ask for SOC2 reports and pen test results — fine to provide redacted reports under NDA.
   - Avoid committing to specific future certifications (e.g., ISO) — provide current state and roadmap.

6) Export / Sanctions (LOW-MED)
   - Standard: comply with export laws. Resist customer requests to audit our export compliance program beyond standard questionnaires.

7) Termination / Transition Assistance (LOW)
   - Transition assistance limited to X weeks and at a professional services rate. Avoid open-ended obligations.

8) Audit Rights (MEDIUM)
   - Customer requests broad audit rights into our systems — push back. Offer annual compliance attestations + read-only access to relevant logs under a redacted/controlled process.

Negotiation playbook / fallback positions:
- Must-haves (deal breakers if not acceptable): liability cap <= 12 months fees, no broad customer indemnity for outputs, no license to our models/weights, limited audit scope.
- Concession candidates: minor SLA percentage increases; one-time compliance walkthrough; additional service credits if SLA is aggressive.
- Creative alternatives: add performance-based routing clause (we will route to pre-agreed fallback model under capacity constraints) and document expected latencies — reduces SLA pressure.

Suggested edits (language snippets to propose):
- "Limitation of Liability: Except for liability arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, either party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim."
- "License to Outputs: Customer is granted a limited, non-exclusive, perpetual license to use Outputs for internal business purposes and to provide services to its end customers, but no license is granted to any Redwood Inference model weights, training data, or derivative model artifacts."
- "Indemnity carveout: Customer shall not be entitled to indemnification for claims arising from (i) Customer's combination of Outputs with third-party data or software; or (ii) Customer modifications to Outputs that materially contribute to the alleged claim."

Practical negotiation notes / tactics:
- Start with 12-month cap, but prepare to move to 18 months if AE pushes for commercial consistency; require reciprocal commitments (customer liability for breach of confidentiality).
- Use reference customers: cite similar customers where we maintained 12-month cap + limited indemnity.
- If they push for model retraining rights, offer a paid professional-services engagement + clear data handling and IP terms.
- For SLA: offer pilot SLA for first 6 months (measurement period) with conservative credits; re-evaluate after maturity.

Stakeholders to loop in during redlines:
- Legal: Olivia Wright (primary), Maya Patel (DPA specialist)
- Product/Eng: Ethan Kim (SRE), Priya Desai (serving-runtime lead) — for SLA realism and fallback model statements
- Sales/CS: AE (named in email thread), Customer Success manager (for churn risk assessment)
- Finance: confirm acceptable cap numbers and revenue impact modeling

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether customer requires KMS-managed keys (customer-managed). If yes, confirm support matrix and any professional services needed.
- Get SRE input on realistic availability numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted for customer's region (EU). Action: ping Ethan + Priya.
- Check whether this customer is a strategic reference; if yes, consider small cap concession in exchange for reference commitment.

Negotiation timeline suggestion:
- T+0: Send redlines with proposed language (legal + AE loop).
- T+3 business days: expect counter from customer legal.
- T+7 business days: internal review of counters and finalize positions with Product/SRE.
- T+10-14 business days: sign if concessions acceptable; else escalate to Head of Revenue for approval.

Notes to self (scratchpad items):
- Pull last closed enterprise CMA to copy concession language (filename: customer-master-agreement-acme-closed-2025.docx).
- Draft quick 1-pager for AE summarizing negotiation points and trade-offs (will help close loop).
- Validate whether the Confluence compliance doc has updated SOC2 scope post-Nov 2025.

Mini checklists to include in outgoing redline email:
- Highlight: liability cap request + rationale (small % revenue exposure), indemnity carveout bullets, DPA constraints on model retraining, SLA measurement & remedies limited to credits, request for SOC2 under NDA only.
- Attach: redline document (changes tracked), short executive summary, SRE note on SLA realism.

End of scratchpad.

(Notes: keep iterative — this is living. Will move to in_review when I have Product/SRE alignment.)
